messages.author: 1ff0fd8a3a9b92e7
messages.subject: Assigning specific colour_hue to specific variable
parts:
Hi all:

My name is Eric; I am a Biostatistics student at UNC. I am really
struggling to assign colors to a specific variable in ggplot2; for
instance, in the below (trivial) example, the labels are used to
assign colors for the bar graph; how do I specifically assign
label="a" to be the "pinkish" default colour_hue, while the "c" to be,
for instance, the "turquoise" color from colour_hue? This is
important because I need certain colors to be consistent across plots
for a paper. Second, how do I assign a colour_hue color specifically
for the vertical line? (It needs to match the color of one of the
bars from the graph.)

Thank you for all your terrific work on this package. I urgently
await your response!

Eric Butter

**************

library(grDevices)
library(ggplot2)

value <- c(0,1,2,3)
labels <- c("a", "b", "c", "d")
data <- as.data.frame(cbind(nums, name))

#finding the median of a subset of the data and making a vertical line
from it
med <- as.numeric(median(as.vector(subset(data, grepl("c", labels))
$value)))

png(filename="tmppic.png")
ggplot(data, aes(x=data$value, fill=data$labels))+geom_bar()
+stat_bin(binwidth=0.01)+geom_vline(xintercept=med)
dev.off()

**************

messages.subject: Re: Assigning specific colour_hue to specific variable
parts:
Hi:

Try something like this:

value <- c(0,1,2,3)
labels <- c("a", "b", "c", "d")
data <- as.data.frame(cbind(value, labels))
med <- as.numeric(median(as.vector(subset(data, grepl("c", labels))$value)))

ggplot(data, aes(x=data$value, fill=data$labels)) + geom_bar() +
   geom_vline(xintercept=med, size = 1.5) + scale_fill_manual(values =
        c('a' = 'red', 'b' = 'blue', 'c' = 'yellow', 'd' = 'green'))

Substitute your desired colors in place of the ones given above.

HTH,
Dennis

PS: For future reference, put your + signs at the end of a line rather
than the beginning, especially if you want folks to copy and paste your
code into their sessions.

parts:
Hello again:

I have a couple follow-up questions related to the same example
below. I think these are a little trickier than my last question
(hopefully that is a good thing!) :)

First, if I want to use geom_text() to label my geom_vline() but the
potential y axes (data$value) for my real dataset vary by orders of
magnitude from plot to plot, how can I flexibly label the geom_vline()
such that the label always appears a reasonable (say, 75% of y_max)
height above the x-axis? (I understand from the website that both x
*and* y need to be specified.)

Secondly, how can I make this geom_text() label include both text and
a variable calculated within the R script (in this case, for instance,
"Median = " + med)? Finally, is there any way for me to send an
"arrow" or "ruler" of some kind from the y-axis to each individual bar
-- i.e., not all the way across the screen like in geom_hline()?
(This last question is not really referring to this example, but
rather a geom_point() plot, if it makes any difference.)

Thanks again for your help and patience! Eric Butter, UNC
Biostatistics

library(grDevices)
library(ggplot2)

value <- c(0,1,2,3)
labels <- c("a", "b", "c", "d")
data <- as.data.frame(cbind(value, labels))

#finding the median of a subset of the data and making a vertical line
from it

med <- as.numeric(median(as.vector(subset(data, grepl("c", labels))
$value)))

png(filename="tmppic.png")
ggplot(data, aes(x=data$value, fill=data$labels))

+geom_bar(binwidth=0.01)+
geom_vline(xintercept=med)
dev.off()
